# Delaware statute of limitations — 3 years; tolling

*Citation:* 10 Del. C. §8106; *Wal-Mart v. AIG Life*, 860 A.2d 312 (Del. 2004) (tolling doctrines); laches in Chancery  
*Status in this library:* in force

Contract and fiduciary claims: **three years** from accrual (Chancery applies the statute by analogy via laches). Tolling: (1) inherently unknowable injury; (2) fraudulent concealment (affirmative acts of concealment); (3) equitable tolling where a fiduciary relationship exists and the plaintiff reasonably relied — **equitable tolling under the fiduciary rationale is weaker where fiduciary duties are contractually eliminated**, but a contractual duty to disclose (§5.4's 30-day notice) that was breached supports concealment-based tolling as to the undisclosed fees.
===TOOLEY===
# Direct vs derivative claims — Tooley; demand futility

*Citation:* *Tooley v. Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette*, 845 A.2d 1031 (Del. 2004); *United Food & Commercial Workers v. Zuckerberg*, 262 A.3d 1034 (Del. 2021); 6 Del. C. §18-1001 to 18-1003  
*Status in this library:* in force

A claim is derivative if the **company** suffered the harm and would receive the benefit of recovery (e.g., excessive fees paid to an affiliate); it is direct if the member suffered harm independent of the company (e.g., wrongful dilution of the member's own interest, or breach of a contractual right personal to the member). Derivative claims in an LLC require demand on the manager or pleaded futility (§18-1001; *Zuckerberg* test) — futility is readily pleaded where the sole manager is the interested party.

10: ## 0. Client answers — 2026-10-08

12: Answers received (record in `QUESTIONS.md`; the client has **no further information** on the unanswered items, which are re-flagged as open items). Four facts now confirmed:

14: 1. **The call arrived by text only.** Castellan texted her the PDF on 2026-08-20; no letter or certified mail ever came; the email address in the Company's records is from 2019 and dead. 19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. Bottom line
22: 
23: **Reject the $189,100. Do not sign anything. Sue in Delaware Chancery — but not for breach of fiduciary duty in the way the client wants.**
24: 
25: The client's instinct ("he's looting the company") points at the wrong claim. OA §7.3 eliminates the Manager's fiduciary duties, and Delaware validates that elimination. What survives is **contract**: the affiliate-transaction conditions in §5.4, and — far more valuable — the **notice and valuation conditions in §6.3** that the dilution depended on. The dilution to 6.1% looks invalid on the face of the documents, and if it is invalid, the Company has **no §9.2 option at all**, because that option arises only "following a Dilution Event."

27: Money at stake, per `valuation_gap.json`:
28: 
29: | Outcome | Value to client |
30: |---|---|
31: | The offer as made (6.1% × $3.1M book) | **$189,100** |
32: | Dilution redone at a good-faith fair value (15.61%), then bought at book | $483,929 |
33: | Dilution void, interest held at 18%, bought at book | $558,000 |
34: | Dilution void, interest valued at the independent indication (18% × $9.8M) | **$1,764,000** |

36: Realistic objective: a **negotiated full exit anchored on the $1,764,000 fair-value number**, supported by a filed Chancery action. Litigation leverage is worth roughly **$1.17M–$1.57M** over the offer; the looting claim by itself is worth only about **$121,500** to her (see §5).

38: ---
39: 
40: ## 2. What the waiver actually takes away
41: 
42: OA §7.3: "To the fullest extent permitted by the Delaware Limited Liability Company Act, the Manager shall not owe any fiduciary duties (including the duties of care and loyalty)… the Manager's duties are solely those expressly set forth in this Agreement; provided that nothing herein eliminates the implied contractual covenant of good faith and fair dealing."
43: 
44: 6 Del. C. §18-1101(c) gives "maximum effect to the principle of freedom of contract" and permits duties, *including fiduciary duties*, to be "expanded or restricted or eliminated." So:
45: 
46: - **A duty-of-loyalty/self-dealing claim against Castellan *as Manager* is gone.** Pleading it first invites dismissal.
47: - **What §7.3 does not obviously cover is Castellan *as an 82% Member*.** The excerpt waives the duties of "the Manager," not of Members, and §18-1101(c) eliminates duties only "by provisions in the limited liability company agreement." If the **complete** agreement has no member-level waiver, a controlling-member loyalty claim is available (see `claims.json` #4). **[unverified]** whether Delaware enforces that capacity line as strictly as the text implies — that proposition is not in the library. This is why QUESTIONS.md asks for the full agreement before we plead it.
48: - **The implied covenant cannot be eliminated** (§18-1101(c) proviso; §18-1101(e) also bars exculpation for a *bad-faith* violation of it), and §7.3 expressly preserves it. That is the doctrinal hinge of this case, because §6.3 hands the Manager three exercises of discretion — purpose, delivery, and "fair value … in good faith" — and the library says exactly this kind of discretion is policed for arbitrary or bad-faith exercise (*Dieckman*; *Zimmerman*).

51: ## 3. The case you can actually bring

The 2026-08-20 call went by **text message** with a PDF; **no certified mail was sent**; the email **bounced** to an old address on file. Note what is *not* wrong: 2026-08-20 → 2026-09-20 is **31 days**, so the "at least 30 days" requirement was met. Don't waste the pleading on timing. The client has confirmed every delivery fact (§0), but has also confirmed she **read the PDF 31 days before the due date** — see §7 risk 2 for the candid risk discussion.
56: 2. **Purpose.** §6.3 requires "a bona fide Company purpose set forth in the call notice." The notice said "working capital **and opportunities**." Bram then funded the entire $1,500,000 — including her $270,000 — and declared a Dilution Event five days after the due date, then offered book value six days later. Provable pretext, if the bank records show the money was not needed or not used as stated. Medium strength pending the ledger.
57: 3. **Arbitrary fair value.** §6.3's "fair value … as determined by the Manager in good faith" produced **$7,200,000** against a **2026-10-05 independent indication of $9,800,000 equity / $14,500,000 EV** — **26.53%** and **50.34%** below those figures. The library makes such a determination reviewable for arbitrariness "e.g., a value far below a contemporaneous independent indication." And **6.1% cannot be reproduced from any pro rata formula using $7,200,000** (the value-weighted computation gives 14.90%; the independent value gives 15.61%; book weighting gives 12.13%; exactly 6.1% would require fair value of **$768,908**). That unexplained number is our best exhibit.
58: 
59: *Tooley*: wrongful dilution of the member's own interest is **direct**, so the client sues in her own name, needs no demand, and any recovery comes to **her**, not to the Company she must then share 82% of with Castellan.
60: 
61: **Bucket B — the affiliate fees (derivative, secondary).** §5.4 permits affiliate transactions **only if** (i) terms are "no less favorable … than … arm's-length" and (ii) any transaction with payments over $50,000/yr is **disclosed in writing to all Members within 30 days**. 63: **Bucket C — declarations that stop the buyout.** No valid Dilution Event ⇒ no §9.2 option ⇒ the Company cannot force a sale at $189,100. Also get a declaration on how the $270,000 Castellan paid "for" her was booked (contribution vs. loan to her — see §7, risk 5).
64: 
65: ## 4. Limitations — real, and mostly manageable
66: 
67: 10 Del. C. §8106: **three years**; Chancery applies it by analogy through laches. Measured from today (2026-10-08) the window opens **2023-10-08**.
68: 
69: - Dilution/buyout conduct (Aug–Oct 2026): **safe**.
70: - Affiliate fees, each payment a separate accrual: **$675,000 inside** (2024, 2025, 2026) and **$375,000 outside** (2022-09-01 $180k + 2023-09-01 $195k = 35.7% of the total). A challenge to the **2022-08-15 engagement itself** expired 2025-08-15.

72: - **The client must look diligent and prompt.** She confirms she learned of Castellan in 2026; the broker opinion is dated 2026-10-05. Filing within weeks is important both for tolling credibility and against laches.
73: - **Unknown:** the monthly 6% fees are unquantified, so the barred portion of that component cannot be computed (see QUESTIONS.md). Do not state a total fee number in any pleading until the gross-rent figures are in.
74: 
75: ## 5. Why the "looting" claim is not the case
